opportunities.title: Stories, essays, thinkpieces and rants
opportunities.excerpt: Afrolicious pays $75 for stories, essays, thinkpieces and rants of 600–800 words. Official eligibility is Black Africans and Black African diasporas.

eligibility.summary: Black Africans and Black African diasporas. Nigeria qualifies. This is not a worldwide open call.

pay.conditions: Official pitching page: $75 for stories, essays, thinkpieces and rants between 600 and 800 words. Page design/development is a separate $75 rate. Other formats are paid at a fair and agreed-upon rate — that rate is not stated as a fixed number.

whatTheyWant: Work at the intersection of the Africas and its diasporas. Afrolicious centers Blackness and Black Africanness.
Stories, essays, thinkpieces and rants of 600–800 words.

A pitch by email that includes: a 140-character thesis; one or two paragraphs describing the piece; three or four sources (potential sources count); a link to your website or blog; any ideas for the article design.
A personal website or blog outside social media is not required, but the publication says it prioritizes people who arrive with their own platform, regardless of size.
whatTheyDontWant: The official pitching page does not list genre exclusions beyond the formats it names.
AI policy is not stated on the official pitching page.
opportunities.rights: Not publicly stated on the official pitching page.
howToSubmit: Email hello@afrolicious.com with the pitch details listed above.
The official page says they will get back to you within two weeks.

opportunities.title: Personal Essay
opportunities.seoTitle: The Republic Personal Essay submissions: ₦100,000 for 2,001–3,000 words
opportunities.excerpt: The Republic pays ₦100,000 for Personal Essays of 2,001–3,000 words. Submit through the official account form. Other categories have their own rates on the official submissions page.
opportunities.applyMethod: Official submissions form (sign in or create an account)

eligibility.summary: The official submissions page does not state a nationality restriction. Personal essays should speak to questions shaping Nigerian and African life. Do not read that as a closed country list.

pay.conditions: This figure is the official Personal Essay fee only. The Republic states that rates vary by format, length and editorial demands. Other listed categories (Analysis & Opinion, Expert Commentary, Fiction, Deep Dive, Interview, Photo Essay, Profile, Review – Regular, Review – Extended, Reportage, The Black Atlantic) have their own rates on the official page. Those other rates are not copied here because they are not shown as a single static table on the current page. Check the official submissions page before pitching another category.
pay.timing: Payment is processed within 30 days of publication. After publication you receive an invoice request by email and are paid through your preferred method.

whatTheyWant: Personal essays that combine strong writing with clear insight, reflection and relevance to broader questions shaping Nigerian and African life.
The magazine publishes journalism, essays, criticism and fiction grounded in intellectual seriousness, strong reporting and clarity of thought.
whatTheyDontWant: AI policy is not stated on the official submissions page.
Do not treat the Personal Essay rate as the rate for every Republic category.
requirements: Sign in or create an account on The Republic
Use Submissions and complete the official form
Pitch through that form — the FAQ does not invite email pitches
opportunities.rights: Not publicly stated on the official submissions page.
howToSubmit: Go to https://rpublc.com/submissions
Log in or create an account.
Open Submissions and complete the form. Editors contact you if the piece is a fit.

opportunities.title: 8th edition — poetry, short story, essay
opportunities.seoTitle: Efiko Magazine submissions (8th edition): poetry, stories and essays
opportunities.excerpt: Efiko is accepting poetry, short stories and essays for its 8th edition until 30 August 2026. Nigerian-account contributors are paid ₦20,000 or ₦30,000 depending on length. Work sent outside the window is deleted unread.

eligibility.summary: Writers of African origin based anywhere in the world, or anyone writing about Africa.

pay.conditions: For contributors with a Nigerian bank account: ₦30,000 for 2 or more poems, or for prose over 2,500 published words; ₦20,000 for accepted submissions below those thresholds. Paid upon publication. Contributors with non-Nigerian bank accounts currently receive a novel or nonfiction book by a selected African author if Amazon delivers to their country, value capped at $35 including processing — not a cash fee. Do not describe Efiko as paying every contributor ₦30,000.

wordCount.notes: Poetry is specified as 2 to 5 poems totalling 10 pages, not a word count. The numeric min/max stored here is the official short-story and essay range.

whatTheyWant: Poems, short stories and essays of high quality from writers of African origin anywhere, or from people writing about Africa.
Times New Roman, 12pt, double-spaced, numbered pages.
One piece per issue.
A 5-line bio in the email body.
whatTheyDontWant: Work sent outside the submission window is deleted unread.
Except in special cases, only original, previously unpublished work. Work that already exists online is not accepted.
More than one piece per issue.
Submissions that do not name the genre in the email subject line are not read.
Extensive revision after acceptance is not allowed. Title decisions are final.
requirements: Times New Roman 12pt, double-spaced, numbered pages
opportunities.rights: First serial rights; rights to republish in a collection; shared rights for maiden adaptations. Text rights revert to the writer 90 days after publication. If you reprint or repurpose the work, you must acknowledge Efiko as first publisher.
howToSubmit: Email a Word document to submissions@efikomag.com.
Put the genre in the subject line.
Name the file with your name and the genre.
Include a 5-line bio in the email body.
Simultaneous submissions are allowed; notify Efiko promptly if accepted elsewhere.
If you have no response after 3 months, the official page says to inquire at editors@efikomag.com.

opportunities.title: African mythology, folklore and cultural memory
opportunities.seoTitle: Oriire submissions: African mythology and folklore (₦10,000 / bonus ₦15,000)
opportunities.excerpt: Oriire pays ₦10,000 per accepted article (₦5,000 per codex entry). A temporary ₦15,000 bonus applies to Encounters, Folktales & Narrative Retellings and Listicles through 22 August 2026. AI-generated writing and images are prohibited.

eligibility.summary: The official submissions page does not state a nationality restriction. The subject matter must be African mythology, folklore and cultural memory, tied to a specific ethnic group, culture, region or historical period.

opportunities.writingTypeLabel: Long-form, folktales, essays, interviews, heritage reviews, listicles, encounters

pay.conditions: Standard official rates: ₦10,000 per accepted article and ₦5,000 per accepted codex entry. Temporary bonus through 22 August 2026: ₦15,000 per accepted submission in Encounters, Folktales & Narrative Retellings, or Listicles. After that date the standard rates apply. Payment details are requested on the submission form. Contributors handle their own tax obligations.
pay.timing: The official page says you get paid when the story is published. A more specific number of days is not stated.

whatTheyWant: Long-form work on African mythology, folklore and cultural memory inside Oriire’s pillars: Mythology; Deities, Spirits & Cosmologies; Folktales, Legends & Oral Traditions; Ancestry, Destiny & Personhood; Festivals, Rituals, Symbols & Sacred Practice; Indigenous Knowledge Systems; Historical Memory & Heritage; Diaspora, Transformation & Survival.
Categories: Long-Form Articles; Folktales & Narrative Retellings; Essays; Interviews & Conversations; Heritage Reviews; Listicles; Encounters.
Specificity is mandatory: tie the piece to a specific ethnic group, culture, region or historical period.
Verifiable or historical claims must be sourced. Oral material may be attributed by provenance (for example “as told by”).
At least one relevant image you have the right to use, with a clear caption.
Voice: research-driven, intellectually grounded, clear. Vivid specific writing is welcome; empty ornament is not.
whatTheyDontWant: AI-generated written content is strictly prohibited. AI-generated images are also prohibited.
Work published elsewhere.
Vague “African culture” pieces that are not tied to a specific people, place or period.
Clichés such as “rich tapestry” and vagueness such as “shrouded in mystery”.
A recipe on its own (foodways need ritual, symbolic or heritage meaning).
General political, economic or film history with no heritage or belief thread.
Repeating a subject already on Oriire without a clearly new angle.
Titles that end with a full stop, or subtitles that begin “This article explores”.
requirements: Create an account and submit through the official portal
At least one captioned image you have rights to
Up to 2 articles and 3 codex entries every 14 days (drafts do not count)
opportunities.rights: Not publicly stated on the official submissions page.
howToSubmit: Create an account via https://oriire.com/join and submit the draft through the official portal.
Editorial review is stated as 1–4 weeks, then an edit pass, then publication and payment.

opportunities.title: Writing Loss & Grief
opportunities.seoTitle: The Lagos Review: Writing Loss & Grief essays — $250
opportunities.excerpt: The Lagos Review is paying $250 per published essay (up to 1,500 words) on loss and grief. Rolling submissions June–December 2026. AI-produced essays and fiction are not considered.

sources.name: The Lagos Review — Call for essay submissions: Writing Loss & Grief (official)

eligibility.summary: The official call does not state a nationality restriction. It is framed around personal experience of loss and grief.

pay.conditions: $250 per published essay, paid one month after publication. Separate additional opportunity: the top 12 published essays may be compiled into a book, with a one-off royalty of $500. That $500 is not the standard essay fee and is not guaranteed to every contributor.

whatTheyWant: Essays up to 1,500 words on loss and grief in all their forms — not only death.

Official examples include: loss of freedom through incarceration, kidnapping or injustice; migration and losing or searching for home; missed opportunities and vanished dreams; pregnancy loss; domestic or intimate partner violence; discrimination by race, tribe or ethnicity; losing a parent, child, partner, friend, or a stranger whose story pierced you.
First-person, honest, specific lived experience.
whatTheyDontWant: AI-produced essays will not be considered.
Fiction will not be considered for this call.
opportunities.rights: Not fully stated. The call notes that the top 12 published essays may be compiled into a book collection with a one-off $500 royalty. Broader rights terms are not on the call page.
howToSubmit: Email your essay to submissions@thelagosreview.ng.
Submissions are received on a rolling basis from June to December 2026.

opportunities.title: Again column
opportunities.seoTitle: Adi Magazine Again column: $300 for a book you return to
opportunities.excerpt: Adi Magazine is paying $300 for Again columns of up to 1,500 words — a pitch about a book you return to. Official page: this column is open on a rolling basis during the June–September 2026 pause that closed other Adi categories.

eligibility.summary: The official submissions page does not list countries. The Again column is addressed to policymakers, activists and politically-engaged writers. That is a subject/role description, not a nationality list.

pay.conditions: Official submissions page: Adi pays $300 for Again columns up to 1,500 words. This rate is for the Again column only. Do not treat it as the rate for Adi essays, interviews, fiction or poetry.

whatTheyWant: A love letter to a treasured text you return to again and again — political texts, poetry, novels or creative nonfiction.
Pitch: the title of the book plus a short summary (2 paragraphs maximum) of why you chose it.
Include 1–2 links to previous work.
Subject line: AGAIN PITCH.
Adi describes itself as a literary magazine of global politics dedicated to rehumanizing policy.
whatTheyDontWant: Attachments unless editors request them.
Submissions or pitches generated with AI.
Work previously published in English.
Hate speech or discriminatory language.
More than one Adi submission at a time — wait until the current one is accepted or declined.
opportunities.rights: Adi acquires first exclusive, world English-language publication rights. Copyright remains with the author.
howToSubmit: Email admin@adimagazine.com with subject AGAIN PITCH.
Do not send an attachment unless an editor asks.
Simultaneous submissions are allowed; withdraw if accepted elsewhere.

AI-generated submissions or pitches.
Work previously published in English.
More than one Adi submission at a time.

opportunities.title: Personal essay
opportunities.seoTitle: Longreads personal essays: $500 for a finished draft
opportunities.excerpt: Longreads pays $500 for personal essays. They do not commission personal essays from a pitch — send a full, polished draft. Official page: writers and journalists around the world. Generative AI is not accepted.

eligibility.summary: Official page: pitches and original nonfiction from writers and journalists around the world. No country list.

pay.conditions: Official page: the rate for personal essays is $500. This is not the rate for reading lists ($350) or reported features (from 50 cents a word).
pay.timing: Net-60. The official page says payment is often processed sooner.

wordCount.display: No hard personal-essay limit stated. Official guideline for most published features: 2,000–6,000 words — a guideline, not a rule.

response.label: They generally only reply if interested

whatTheyWant: A full, polished personal-essay draft. They will not commission a personal essay from a pitch.
Smart, unexpected angles and a compelling voice. Wide range of topics.
Attach PDF, Google Doc or Word, or paste the draft in the email.
Subject line should include the pitch type (“Personal Essay”) and the topic.
They do not accept fiction.
whatTheyDontWant: A personal-essay pitch without a finished draft.
Any submission or pitch written or edited using generative AI tools such as ChatGPT.
Fiction.
requirements: Subject includes Personal Essay and the topic
opportunities.rights: Not publicly stated on the official submissions page.
howToSubmit: Email hello@longreads.com with subject line Personal Essay + topic.
Attach or paste the finished draft.
They cannot confirm receipt. They generally reply only if interested. Simultaneous submissions are encouraged.

eligibility.summary: Official page: original nonfiction from writers and journalists around the world.

pay.conditions: Official page: $350 per reading list. Separate from the $500 personal-essay rate and from reported-feature rates.
pay.timing: Net-60. The official page says payment is often processed sooner.

response.label: They generally only reply if interested

Timely topics, or offbeat and unique angles. A diverse mix of publications and writers.
Subject line: Reading List + topic.
whatTheyDontWant: Reading lists that feature books exclusively. A book as a side note is occasionally fine.
Generative AI writing or editing.
Fiction.
requirements: Subject includes Reading List and the topic

pay.timing: Net-60. The official page says payment is often processed sooner.

Something about you and clips of previously published work.

opportunities.excerpt: Omenana’s official submissions page still says the window closed 15 March 2026. That date has passed. Official pay is $20 per published story. Africa and the African diaspora. Bookmark — do not submit as if it is open.
opportunities.applyMethod: Email when a new window is announced — currently closed

eligibility.summary: Artists and writers from Africa and the African diaspora. The official page points to the African Speculative Fiction Society definition of who is African. Nigeria qualifies. This is not a worldwide open call.

pay.conditions: Official page: Omenana will pay $20 for every story published. Commissioned art is paid depending on budget. The page does not state a separate essay or review fee.

wordCount.display: Short fiction up to 5,000; flash up to 1,000; essays/CNF up to 3,000; reviews 800–2,000
wordCount.notes: Different categories have different official limits. The stored max is the short-fiction ceiling.

deadline.display: Official page: open until 15 March 2026 — that date has passed

whatTheyWant: Speculative fiction and art (fantasy, science fiction, horror or magical realism) involving characters, settings or themes directly related to the African continent.
English (translations welcome). Original, previously unpublished. No fan fiction.
Non-fiction essays or reviews that deal with African speculative fiction.

When a window is open: one email attachment (.doc, .docx, .rtf or .odt) to editor@omenana.com, plus a cover letter with legal name, address, email, phone, brief publication history, bio (max 100 words) and a profile photo.
whatTheyDontWant: Do not submit while the stated window is closed.
Poetry, drama or film scripts.
Simultaneous submissions — the official page says they no longer accept them.
Revised drafts of work already submitted, unless they ask.
Art already published anywhere other than your portfolio, unless they request it.
requirements: Wait for a new official window
opportunities.rights: Not publicly stated on the official submissions page.
howToSubmit: Do not treat the March 2026 window as open.
When a new window is posted on https://omenana.com/omenana-submissions/, email editor@omenana.com as specified there.
